sources.quote: Alpha Reticuli, Latinized from α Reticuli, also named Rhombus, is the brightest star in the southern circumpolar constellation of Reticulum, with an apparent visual magnitude of 3.3.

introduction.text: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 104 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,152 K, so 12.812 solar radii.
